title: S&P Global Investment Manager Index (Sep 2026) — 10:00 ET, the only buy-side risk-appetite survey on this calendar, released on FOMC day one
source: EST: read verbatim off S&P Global's own calendar listing, pmi.spglobal.com/Public/Release/ReleaseDates?language=en, re-fetched direct by this lane 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 23,858 bytes): 'September 15 | 14:00 UTC | S&P Global Investment Manager Index'. 14:00 UTC is 10:00 ET under EDT. INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED BY A DATE RULE DERIVED FROM THREE PRIMARY RELEASES, not by trusting the listing: S&P Global's press-release index (HTTP 200, 92,883 bytes) plus three IMI PDFs fetched direct this session give release dates 2026-01-13 (masthead 'Embargoed until 1000 EST (1500 UTC) 13 January 2026', data collected January 5-8), 2026-05-12 ('1000 EDT (1400 UTC) 12 May 2026', collected May 5-7) and 2026-08-11 ('1000 EDT (1400 UTC) 11 August 2026', collected August 1-7). All three are the Tuesday eight days after that month's first Monday; the same rule applied to September 2026 (first Monday 2026-09-07) yields 2026-09-15 exactly, which is why this edition is a THIRD Tuesday where the others were seconds. Filed estimate on the same standing schema gap the S&P Global PMI entries name — market-events-data.ts defines no confirmed-source prefix for a private survey compiler — and because this lane does not self-confirm. The date is not in doubt; the label is about the taxonomy.
notes: The calendar's only BUY-SIDE forward-looking risk-appetite series. Researched 2026-09-09; canonical file written then from the one proposal that existed (from-sp-global-manufacturing-pmi-2026-10-01), which is now inert. That proposal made two claims and this lane tested both. (1) 'a class this calendar tracks nothing of' — REFINED, not confirmed: 44 tracked titles are surveys, but every one polls an economic actor about its own business or household (Conference Board, UMich, NAHB, Empire/Philly/Dallas, Tankan) or the credit plumbing (SLOOS, SCOOS-2026-09-24 on dealer financing terms). None asks an asset manager what it intends to do with US equities in the next 30 days. The narrow claim survives; the broad one does not. (2) 'its date makes it sharper than its impact tier suggests' — SPLIT. On the tape: refuted twice, by the consumer-confidence chain's exhaustive FOMC-day-one nulls and by this lane's own reading of the one verified IMI release day, 2026-08-11, whose 10:00-10:15 ET window ranked below its own median on 4 of 5 instruments (SPY p7, IWM p12, ^TNX exactly 0.000%) on a day this calendar tracks nothing else. On the information: SUPPORTED and sharpened — the date rule puts this edition's field window in the week of 09-07, making it the first 2026 edition whose panel answered AFTER the month's jobs report (August's own PDF says its panel answered 'before the August jobs report'). NOT A TRADE: symbols is empty, no macro-keyed house playbook, no published consensus exists for a sentiment survey, and the date is estimate. Read it on 09-16 morning as a prior on how positioned the panel already was; attribute nothing on 09-15. REALIZED 2026-09-15, CLOSED OUT 2026-09-16 (docs/research/events/sp-global-investment-manager-index-2026-09-15.md -> ## Outcome). Released exactly as filed: masthead 'Embargoed until 1000 EDT (1400 UTC) 15 September 2026', fetched direct 2026-09-16. Content INVERTED the August prior in one month - 'Equity investor risk appetite slumps in September', Risk Appetite Index lowest since March, half the panel expecting the US market to lose value, central-bank drag worst since late 2023, and the panel's own Fed path flipped from 'up to 50 basis points of rate cuts' (March) to 'up to 50 basis points of hikes are anticipated'; cause stated in the release itself as renewed Middle East conflict, an energy-price spike and rising yields inside the field window. Three registered forward tests scored: FT-1 MIXED (the release states its collection window twice - body '3-10 September', Note to Editors '8-10 September' - though BOTH end Thursday 09-10, so the pre-CPI base case is confirmed and the panel never saw CPI 09-11); FT-2 KILLED (the 10:00-10:15 window's share of its own hour EXCEEDED its trailing median on 3 of 4 instruments after the registered guard, so the predicted null failed - a measurement, not an attribution, since 09-15 was broad risk-off on FOMC day one); FT-3 CONFIRMED to the minute (the publisher's calendar rolled and lists the October edition on 2026-10-13 at 14:00 UTC, exactly as the first-Monday-plus-eight rule predicted, taking it to 5 for 5). STATUS UNCHANGED at estimate and the reason is still taxonomy, not date doubt: CONFIRMED_PREFIX was re-read 2026-09-16 and still has no slot for a private survey compiler, even though the publisher's own masthead now confirms the date. Still not a trade, and this entry is closed.
